title: Unfiltered support_tenant retrieval bypasses document allowedRoles via retrieval/router.ts and orchestrator/engine.ts
description: Support tenant knowledge documents enforce per-document role ACLs (such as ['staff', 'admin'] and ['admin'], defaulting new documents to ['admin']) to isolate internal staff and executive documentation from customers and external API callers. However, retrieve() in server/src/custom/ai-platform/retrieval/hybrid.ts disables role filtering whenever opts.roles is undefined (allowedRoleSet = null), and both the orchestrator agent context builder (serving external sk-cp- flow callers and edit_flows dry-runs) and the AI Platform retrieval query endpoint (gated only on view_retrieval, not manage_x_gateway) invoke retrieve() on support_tenant scopes without restricting roles or enforcing Support RBAC.
claimed_root_cause: isSupportChunkVisible() and retrieve() in server/src/custom/ai-platform/retrieval/hybrid.ts treat opts?.roles === undefined as allowedRoleSet = null (unrestricted visibility across all enabled support_tenant documents) and pass undefined to searchSupportKnowledgeRanked() in server/src/custom/x-gateway/support-knowledge.ts, while orchestrator/engine.ts:552 omits opts.roles when retrieving support_tenant knowledge for external sk-cp- flow callers (and edit_flows /try dry-runs) and retrieval/router.ts:247,279 allows view_retrieval users lacking manage_x_gateway to query support_tenant scopes with omitted or caller-supplied roles.

trace.description: External sk-cp- API caller granted flow:<slug> invokes /v1/chat/completions (routed through profileInferenceGate at profile-gate.ts:159) and enters executeFlowHttpRequest().

When an agent binds knowledgeScopeKind='support_tenant', buildIsolatedAgentContext invokes deps.retrieve({ kind: agent.knowledgeScopeKind, id: agent.knowledgeScopeId }, userQuery, { signal, respectPillarFlag: true }) with opts.roles omitted (undefined).
Because opts?.roles is undefined on a support_tenant scope, allowedRoleSet evaluates to null instead of restricting visibility to public/wildcard documents.
When allowedRoleSet === null, isSupportChunkVisible returns true for every enabled support_tenant chunk regardless of allowedRoles (including ['admin'] and ['staff', 'admin'] documents).
Restricted support_tenant knowledge chunks returned by retrieve() are wrapped in <reference_data> inside systemSections and pushed into agentCtx.conversation (line 574).

deps.callGateway() sends agentCtx.conversation containing the restricted support_tenant <reference_data> to the model serving the external sk-cp- caller, whose completion is returned via sendText() (line 1755).

evidence.description: profileInferenceGate admits sk-cp- client profile requests targeting flow:<slug> into runPreRequest() when orchestrator is enabled.

searchSupportKnowledgeRanked skips allowedRoles filtering when role === undefined, whereas default Support KB docs define ['staff', 'admin'] (line 198) and ['admin'] (line 209) and upsertSupportKnowledgeDoc defaults new docs to ['admin'] (line 147).

runKeywordSearch passes undefined role to searchSupportKnowledgeRanked when opts.roles === undefined, returning restricted support_tenant documents in both keyword mode and flags.retrieval=false fallback (line 346).
retrieve() adds every chunk's docId into allowedDocIds (checked by searchTopVectors at vector-store.ts:412 and hybrid RRF fusion at hybrid.ts:487) when allowedRoleSet is null.
validateKnowledgeScopePair permits orchestrator agents to configure knowledgeScopeKind='support_tenant' (also exposed at Flows.tsx:1178) without enforcing Support role restrictions at runtime.

POST /api/ai-platform/flows/:id/try requires only edit_flows (not manage_x_gateway) and calls startRun(), allowing a delegated flow editor to dry-run a support_tenant-bound agent without Support RBAC.

POST /api/ai-platform/retrieval/:scopeKind/:scopeId/query requires only view_retrieval (not manage_x_gateway) and forwards caller-controlled req.body.roles (or undefined when omitted) to retrieve() at line 279.

PERMISSION_GATES isolates /api/thruline (including /api/thruline/support/* KB endpoints gated at support-enterprise-router.ts:134-150) under manage_x_gateway separately from /api/ai-platform under manage_ai_platform (line 131; permissions.ts:47 maps query to view_retrieval).
Comparable Support runtime caller passes roles: userContext.role ? [userContext.role] : [] to retrieve(), keeping empty arrays restricted to ['*'] docs rather than passing undefined.

blockers: Approved OS-enforced execution sandbox (isolated loopback namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only target/toolchain mounts, resource limits, and POSIX O_NOFOLLOW promotion) is unavailable on this Windows host, preventing live execution against retrieve(), retrieval/router.ts, and executeFlowHttpRequest().

validation_plan.local: Inside an isolated test sandbox using in-memory SQLite and fake provider/embeddings runners, seed a dummy support_tenant containing an ['admin']-only KB document and verify: (a) POST /api/ai-platform/retrieval/support-tenant/<id>/query authenticated as a delegated member with only ['view_retrieval'] (no manage_x_gateway) returns the ['admin']-only chunk text both when roles is omitted and when roles=['admin']; and (b) invoking POST /api/ai-platform/flows/:id/try as an ['edit_flows']-only user or POST /v1/chat/completions with a dummy sk-cp- key granted flow:<slug> on an agent bound to knowledgeScopeKind='support_tenant' injects the ['admin']-only chunk into <reference_data> and exposes it in the response.
validation_plan.deployment: In a non-destructive read-only inspection of deployed configuration, check whether any delegated non-primary user holds view_retrieval or edit_flows without manage_x_gateway/use_x_gateway, whether flags.orchestrator or flags.retrieval is enabled, and whether any custom_ai_agents row or published custom_ai_flows snapshot references knowledge_scope_kind='support_tenant' on a tenant with role-restricted KB docs.

title: userInferenceGate and profileInferenceGate bypassed via /thruline/v1beta, Gemini header-precedence mismatch, and uppercase /V1BETA query keys
description: `userInferenceGate` enforces per-user RPM caps, daily/monthly usage quotas, and usage attribution/metering on `sk-flm-` and `sk-xgw-` keys, while `profileInferenceGate` enforces client-profile (`sk-cp-`) RPM caps, daily/monthly and end-user quotas, model allowlists, `maxTokens` caps, content/output guards, and attribution. Three mismatches across `server/src/app.ts`, `server/src/custom/register.ts`, `server/src/middleware/user-rate-limit.ts`, and the mounted Gemini routers enable complete gate bypasses: (1) `server/src/custom/register.ts:283` mounts `custom/x-gateway/gemini-router.ts` on `/thruline/v1beta` (and `/x/v1beta` via `server/src/custom/legacy-gateway-path.ts:7`), which is omitted from `userInferenceGate` (`register.ts:228`), `/thruline/v1`'s `getConfigSnapshot().enabled` gate (`register.ts:174`), and `app.ts:339`/`358`'s per-IP `createProxyRateLimiter` (and `gemini-router.ts` never checks `enabled`), allowing any `sk-xgw-` or `use_x_gateway`-holding `sk-flm-` key to run unmetered inference even when Thruline is disabled; (2) on `/v1beta`, `extractInferenceToken` (`user-rate-limit.ts:19-25`) stops at `Authorization` (or `x-api-key`) before inspecting `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=`, whereas `extractGeminiApiKey` (`gemini-router.ts:47-55`) checks `x-goog-api-key` and `?key=` before `Authorization: Bearer ...`—so `Authorization: Bearer dummy` alongside `x-goog-api-key: <sk-xgw- | use_x_gateway sk-flm->` (or `?key=...`) passes `userInferenceGate` unmetered and executes in `custom/x-gateway/gemini-router.ts`; (3) `extractInferenceToken` (`user-rate-limit.ts:22`) checks `req.originalUrl.startsWith('/v1beta')` case-sensitively before reading `req.query.key`, whereas Express leaves `case sensitive routing` disabled by default (`app.ts:113`), so `/V1BETA/models/...:generateContent?key=<sk-flm- | sk-xgw- | sk-cp->` causes `extractInferenceToken` to return `undefined` in both `userInferenceGate` and `profileInferenceGate` (`profile-gate.ts:38-39`) before executing via `custom/x-gateway/gemini-router.ts` (`sk-xgw-` / `use_x_gateway` `sk-flm-`) or falling through to `server/src/routes/gemini.ts:59,239` (any `sk-flm-` or `sk-cp-`).
claimed_root_cause: register.ts omits /thruline/v1beta from userInferenceGate and the Thruline enabled gate, and extractInferenceToken diverges from the Gemini routers on credential header precedence and case-sensitive /v1beta query-key matching.

trace.description: Invokes registerCustomRoutes(app) with Express case-insensitive routing enabled by default (line 113), after legacyGatewayPath (/x -> /thruline rewrite at line 129) and JSON body parsing (lines 224 and 227), and before /thruline/v1 and /v1beta proxy rate limiters (lines 339 and 358) and routes/gemini.ts (line 359).

Mounts userInferenceGate on ['/v1', '/v1beta', '/thruline/v1'] (omitting /thruline/v1beta) and profileInferenceGate on ['/v1', '/v1beta'] (line 240), while mounting custom/x-gateway/gemini-router.ts on /v1beta (line 282) and /thruline/v1beta (line 283) outside /thruline/v1's enabled gate (line 174).
Reads req.headers.authorization (line 19) and x-api-key (line 20) before x-goog-api-key (line 21), and only reads req.query.key when req.originalUrl.startsWith('/v1beta') (line 22, case-sensitive).

Calls next() without RPM, quota, or usage enforcement when extractUserKey returns undefined; profileInferenceGate similarly calls next() when extractInferenceToken returns undefined (server/src/middleware/profile-gate.ts:38-39).

Handles /v1beta, /V1BETA, /thruline/v1beta, and /x/v1beta requests using extractGeminiApiKey (lines 47-55, prioritizing x-goog-api-key and ?key= before Authorization) to execute unthrottled and unmetered inference for sk-xgw- and use_x_gateway sk-flm- keys even when disabled; non-X-Gateway keys on /V1BETA fall through at line 184 to server/src/routes/gemini.ts (lines 59 and 239), executing sk-flm- and sk-cp- inference without userInferenceGate or profileInferenceGate enforcement.

evidence.description: Mounts custom/x-gateway/gemini-router.ts on /thruline/v1beta outside userInferenceGate (line 228), outside /thruline/v1's enabled gate (line 174), and outside app.ts:339/358 proxy rate limiters (with /x/v1beta rewritten via server/src/custom/legacy-gateway-path.ts:7).

extractGeminiApiKey checks x-goog-api-key (line 48) and req.query['key'] (line 50) before Authorization Bearer (line 52), opposite extractInferenceToken in server/src/middleware/user-rate-limit.ts:19-22.

Fallback /v1beta Gemini router resolves req.query.key (line 52 and line 59) for sk-cp- and sk-flm- keys when uppercase /V1BETA causes extractInferenceToken to return undefined to userInferenceGate and profileInferenceGate (server/src/middleware/profile-gate.ts:38-39).

Express mounts /v1beta routers case-insensitively by default (app.ts:113, register.ts:282, app.ts:358-359) while extractInferenceToken checks req.originalUrl.startsWith('/v1beta') case-sensitively (server/src/middleware/user-rate-limit.ts:22).

profileInferenceGate relies solely on extractInferenceToken(req) and calls next() on line 39 when undefined, skipping RPM, quota, allowlist, maxTokens, content filter, output guard, and profile attribution on /V1BETA?... requests.

blockers: Target code execution is omitted on this Windows host (lacks OS-enforced execution sandbox with isolated loopback network namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only target/tool mounts, scratch-only writes, resource/wall-clock limits, and POSIX O_NOFOLLOW promotion), blocking live Express middleware and Gemini router integration verification.

validation_plan.local: Inside an OS-enforced sandbox with an in-memory SQLite DB, mocked upstream provider fetch, X Gateway disabled then enabled, and dummy keys configured with strict 1 RPM and 1 daily-request quotas (plus a restricted sk-cp- key with allowedModels and maxTokens), send bounded loopback HTTP requests to: (1) POST /thruline/v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent (and /x/v1beta/...) with x-goog-api-key: <sk-xgw- or use_x_gateway sk-flm-> while X Gateway is disabled and repeatedly while enabled; (2) POST /v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent with Authorization: Bearer dummy and x-goog-api-key: <sk-xgw- or use_x_gateway sk-flm-> (or ?key=...); and (3) POST /V1BETA/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent?key=<member sk-flm- | sk-xgw- | sk-cp-> with a disallowed model and oversized maxOutputTokens. Confirm 200 responses past the 1 RPM/quota limits, missing X-RateLimit-*-User-RPM and X-RateLimit-*-Profile-RPM headers, un-incremented custom_usage_counters and user_monthly_usage rows, and NULL user_id / profile_id in requests.

title: Unredacted password-reset code logged via console.log lets view_server_logs callers reset the Primary Admin password
description: When legacy password reset is active (getExternalAuthConfig().legacyResetAllowed, true when PUBLIC_APP_URL is unset/empty or FREEAPI_DESKTOP=1 per server/src/services/external-auth-config.ts:25), unauthenticated POST /api/auth/forgot-password (server/src/routes/auth.ts:342) enforces only userCount() > 0 and a 10-second cooldown before calling generateResetCode(accountEmail()) at line 355. generateResetCode (server/src/lib/reset-code.ts:22) prints '  Password-reset code: ' + code via console.log using a 10-character alphanumeric code (server/src/lib/one-time-code.ts:13). At boot, installLogRedaction() (server/src/index.ts:34) wraps console.log and passes strings through redactSecrets() before calling recordConsoleLine (server/src/lib/log-redaction.ts:170) and forwarding to console-stream-router.ts (which hooks console.log at import time via initConsoleLogCapture() at line 145). However, PATTERNS in server/src/lib/log-redaction.ts neither include 'code' in the key-value regex (line 61; 'Password-reset code:' also prevents \bpassword\b\s*[:=] from matching) nor match 10-character codes in the 32+ character fallback (line 83), and NOISE_RE (server/src/lib/server-logs.ts:80) does not filter it. Consequently, the plaintext reset code is exposed via GET /api/logs (server/src/routes/logs.ts:56, gated on delegable 'view_server_logs' in server/src/custom/permission-actions.ts:60) and GET /api/translator/console-logs and /console-logs/stream (server/src/custom/x-gateway/console-stream-router.ts:159,239, gated on 'use_x_gateway' + 'view_server_logs'). A non-primary user holding view_server_logs (documented in shared/permissions.ts:56 as reading redacted diagnostics) can retrieve the code and call POST /api/auth/reset-password -> resetUserPassword (server/src/services/auth.ts:218-228, selecting SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 1), overwriting the Primary Admin password, revoking existing sessions, and obtaining a Primary Admin ('*') session token.
claimed_root_cause: generateResetCode logs a 10-character one-time password-reset credential via console.log without log-redaction coverage or log-viewer exclusion, and GET /api/logs (view_server_logs) and GET /api/translator/console-logs (/stream, use_x_gateway + view_server_logs) expose captured console output to delegated non-primary accounts, enabling Primary Admin takeover via resetUserPassword.

trace.description: Unauthenticated endpoint invokes generateResetCode(accountEmail()) at line 355 when userCount() > 0 and externalAuthRouter (server/src/routes/external-auth.ts:95-97) allows legacy reset.
Generates a 10-character reset code via createOneTimeCode().generate() and writes plaintext '  Password-reset code: ' + code (and '  Account email: ' + accountEmail at line 23) through console.log.

PATTERNS omit 'code' from the key-value regex (line 61) and require 32+ characters in the bare token fallback (line 83), leaving the 10-character code unredacted when recordConsoleLine (line 170) stores it in server-logs.ts and line 171 forwards it to console-stream-router.ts.

Returns the unredacted 'info' entry containing the reset code to any authenticated user granted view_server_logs (also exposed via GET /api/translator/console-logs and /console-logs/stream in server/src/custom/x-gateway/console-stream-router.ts:159,239 to use_x_gateway + view_server_logs holders).

Verifies the disclosed resetCode via resetCodeMatches (line 371) and calls resetUserPassword (server/src/services/auth.ts:218-228, selecting SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 1), overwriting the Primary Admin password hash and returning a Primary Admin ('*') session token at lines 384-385.

evidence.description: installLogRedaction() runs at boot before main(), tapping console.log into server-logs.ts (via log-redaction.ts:170) and forwarding redacted arguments to console-stream-router.ts.
CODE_LENGTH = 10 defines 10-character uppercase alphanumeric codes, below the 32-character minimum of log-redaction.ts:83.
PERMISSION_GATES mounts requireAuth + requireActionPermission('view_logs') on /api/logs ahead of logsRouter.
GET /api/logs requires only the delegable 'view_server_logs' permission (documented in shared/permissions.ts:56 as reading redacted diagnostic messages).

initConsoleLogCapture() (lines 85-129, called at line 145) buffers console output and serves it via /console-logs/stream (line 159) and /console-logs (line 239) to callers with use_x_gateway and view_server_logs (lines 154-155).
resetUserPassword queries SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 1, updates that account's password_hash (line 222), and deletes its sessions (line 223), targeting the Primary Admin created at setup.
RBAC protections (lines 89, 121, 154, 169) prohibit non-primary users and secondary admins from modifying or revoking the Primary Admin (is_primary=1) account.
externalAuthRouter gates /forgot-password and /reset-password behind getExternalAuthConfig().legacyResetAllowed, returning HTTP 410 only when legacyResetAllowed is false.
legacyResetAllowed evaluates to !env('PUBLIC_APP_URL') || process.env.FREEAPI_DESKTOP === '1', remaining true on local/Docker installs without PUBLIC_APP_URL and on desktop installs.

blockers: Live runtime reproduction is disabled on this Windows host because it lacks the required OS-enforced execution sandbox (isolated loopback namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only target/tool mounts, resource caps, and POSIX O_NOFOLLOW promotion).

Exploitability in a deployed instance depends on runtime configuration (PUBLIC_APP_URL unset/empty or FREEAPI_DESKTOP=1 so getExternalAuthConfig().legacyResetAllowed is true) and whether any non-primary account holds view_server_logs (or view_logs).

validation_plan.local: Inside an approved OS-enforced sandbox on a clean disposable SQLite DB with installLogRedaction() active and legacyResetAllowed=true (PUBLIC_APP_URL unset), seed a dummy Primary Admin (userId=1) and a dummy delegated user holding only ['view_server_logs'], send POST /api/auth/forgot-password, read GET /api/logs as the delegated user (and optionally GET /api/translator/console-logs when also granted 'use_x_gateway' with X-Gateway enabled) to observe the unredacted 'Password-reset code:' string, and verify that POST /api/auth/reset-password with that code sets a new password and returns a Primary Admin session token (userId=1) while invalidating prior sessions.
validation_plan.deployment: Non-destructive owner check on the target environment: query GET /api/auth/methods (or check PUBLIC_APP_URL and FREEAPI_DESKTOP env configuration) to verify whether legacyResetAllowed is true, and review GET /api/admin/users as Primary Admin to verify whether any non-primary account has been granted view_server_logs, view_logs, or '*'.

title: Workflow-level write permissions and Apple metadata secrets exposed to pull_request builds
description: .github/workflows/desktop-release.yml declares workflow-level `permissions: contents: write` while running both `build` and `macos-release` on `pull_request` events touching `desktop/**` or the workflow file without `persist-credentials: false` on `actions/checkout@v7.0.1` (which stores `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `$RUNNER_TEMP` via `.git/config` `includeIf`). Subsequent runner-host steps execute PR-modifiable scripts, tests, bundles, and `electron-builder` hooks (`afterPack`, `afterSign`), and the `Package installer` step unconditionally binds five Apple metadata secrets (`APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_KEYCHAIN`, `APPLE_KEYCHAIN_PROFILE`) without a tag or non-PR gate (the sensitive private signing materials `MACOS_CSC_LINK`, `MACOS_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, and `APPLE_API_KEY_P8` remain gated behind `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')`). Additionally, `.github/workflows/docker.yml` sets workflow-level `permissions: packages: write` on `pull_request` runs with persisted `GITHUB_TOKEN`, though GHCR login/push and the `merge` job are gated off on `pull_request` and `Dockerfile` executes in BuildKit without `$RUNNER_TEMP`.
claimed_root_cause: Workflow-level write `permissions`, default `actions/checkout` credential persistence, and unconditional step `env:` secret bindings are not restricted away from `pull_request` jobs that execute contributor-modifiable code.

trace.description: Pull requests modifying `desktop/**` or `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` trigger the `build` and `macos-release` jobs because neither job restricts `github.event_name` or `github.ref`.

Top-level `permissions: contents: write` applies to `build` and `macos-release` on `pull_request` runs (only `publish` at line 516 and release-attachment steps at lines 440 and 496 check `refs/tags/`).

`actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1` (v7.0.1) runs without `persist-credentials: false`, persisting `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: write` on non-downgraded PR runs) under `$RUNNER_TEMP` linked from `.git/config` before PR-controlled scripts, tests, and builds run (lines 104, 138, 146, 152, 157-162).

`APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_KEYCHAIN`, and `APPLE_KEYCHAIN_PROFILE` are bound unconditionally from `secrets.*` on `pull_request` runs and remain in the environment whenever non-empty (lines 331-333).

Runner-host execution invokes PR-modifiable `desktop/scripts/retry-network-step.sh` and `electron-builder` (which executes `afterPack` and `afterSign` scripts from `desktop/electron-builder.yml`) with the persisted `GITHUB_TOKEN` accessible on disk and any configured `APPLE_*` env vars.

evidence.description: Workflow-level `permissions: contents: write` grants write token scope to `build` (line 41) and `macos-release` (line 467) during `pull_request` runs.

`Package installer` binds `secrets.APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `secrets.APPLE_API_ISSUER` (lines 319-323), `secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `secrets.APPLE_KEYCHAIN`, and `secrets.APPLE_KEYCHAIN_PROFILE` without `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')` or `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`.

`macos-release` lacks `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')`, runs `actions/checkout` without `persist-credentials: false` (line 473), and executes `desktop/scripts/retry-network-step.sh` and `desktop/scripts/merge-mac-update-metadata.mjs` on `pull_request`.
Configures `afterPack: ./scripts/after-pack-linux-sandbox.mjs` and `afterSign: ./scripts/after-sign-notarize.mjs` (lines 24-25), invoked by `electron-builder` during `Package installer`.

Workflow-level `permissions: packages: write` applies to `pull_request` builds (line 7) with `actions/checkout@v7.0.1` omitting `persist-credentials: false` (line 36), though GHCR login (line 53), image push (line 78), and `merge` (line 98) are disabled on `pull_request` and `Dockerfile` builds in BuildKit without `$RUNNER_TEMP`.

blockers: GitHub Actions downgrades `GITHUB_TOKEN` to read-only and withholds repository secrets on public-repo fork `pull_request` runs and Dependabot PRs; exploitability depends on hosted repository settings outside source: repository visibility and Actions fork-PR token/secret forwarding settings, whether contributors can push same-repo branches (or maintainers stage external PRs on internal branches) with narrower authority than `main`/`v*` tag/release/package/secret admin permissions, whether push rulesets restrict `.github/workflows/**` modifications on PR branches, whether `github-actions[bot]` bypasses branch/tag protections, and whether the five `APPLE_*` secrets are populated without a GitHub Environment gate.
Execution of workflow runs and target code is omitted on this `win32` host because an OS-enforced execution sandbox and external GitHub API access are unavailable.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated disposable fixture repository or offline workflow linter (`actionlint` / `zizmor`) on a sandboxed Linux runner—without contacting production GitHub releases or real signing credentials—verify that `desktop-release.yml` runs `build` and `macos-release` on `pull_request` with `contents: write`, populates git credentials in `$RUNNER_TEMP` via `actions/checkout`, and passes dummy `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`/`APPLE_API_ISSUER`/`APPLE_TEAM_ID`/`APPLE_KEYCHAIN`/`APPLE_KEYCHAIN_PROFILE` values into `Package installer`.
validation_plan.deployment: Inspect the hosted GitHub repository settings (read-only): (1) repository visibility and Settings -> Actions -> General -> Fork pull request workflows (whether fork PRs receive write tokens or secrets, or require approval); (2) Settings -> Collaborators and teams / custom roles (whether lower-trust contributors can open same-repo PRs); (3) Settings -> Rules -> Rulesets and Branch/Tag protection on `main`, `v*`, releases, and `.github/workflows/**` (including whether `github-actions[bot]` has ruleset bypass); and (4) Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions (whether `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_KEYCHAIN`, and `APPLE_KEYCHAIN_PROFILE` are configured).

title: freellmapi doctor probes URLs from untrusted workspace .claude/settings*.json before URL verification and follows redirects
description: Running `freellmapi doctor` (dispatched via `runDoctor` in `cli/src/index.ts` to `diagnose('claude', ...)` by default) resolves `cwd` (`process.cwd()`) and calls `claudeLayers()` in `cli/src/doctor.ts`, which reads `<cwd>/.claude/settings.local.json` and `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` ahead of user `~/.claude/settings.json` and `process.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` without any workspace trust gate or user confirmation. Unless a system-level Claude managed-settings file sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `diagnose()` marks the workspace value effective and immediately calls `probeGateway(effective.value)` before checking `overridden` or `sameGateway(effective.value, options.expectedUrl)`. `probeGateway()` passes `${normalizeUrl(baseUrl)}/livez` to `fetch` without private/loopback/link-local IP restrictions, scheme allowlisting before fetch, or `redirect: 'error'` (which `cli/src/keys.ts` enforces), allowing a malicious repository's `.claude/settings.json` to trigger unprompted outbound requests (disclosing client egress IP and execution context) or follow 3xx redirects to arbitrary loopback, LAN, or cloud-metadata GET endpoints and query paths.
claimed_root_cause: `claudeLayers()` elevates untrusted project-directory `.claude/settings*.json` `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` values without workspace trust gating, and `diagnose()` / `probeGateway()` invokes redirect-following `fetch` before `sameGateway()` or origin/redirect validation.

trace.description: Reads `<cwd>/.claude/settings.local.json` (line 187) and `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` (line 188) `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` via `envBlockUrl()` ahead of user settings (line 191) and process env (line 197), marking `layers[0].effective = true` (line 205) without a workspace trust check.
Calls `probeGateway(effective.value, options.fetchImpl, options.timeoutMs)` before checking `overridden` (line 413) or `sameGateway(effective.value, options.expectedUrl)` (line 430).

Executes `fetchImpl(`${normalizeUrl(baseUrl)}/livez`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) })` with default `redirect: 'follow'`, omitting `redirect: 'error'` and private/loopback IP restrictions.

evidence.description: `runDoctor()` invokes `diagnose(tool, { expectedUrl: rootUrl(options.url), timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs })` for `DOCTOR_TOOLS` (`['claude', 'codex']` by default, line 443) when `command === 'doctor'` (line 490), letting `diagnose()` default `cwd` to `process.cwd()` without a trust gate.

title: ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation script omits 24 encrypted X-Gateway, AI Platform, and Support tables while probeStoredSecrets checks only api_keys
description: The CLI key-rotation tool server/src/scripts/rotate-encryption-key.ts only rotates four ciphertext locations (api_keys.encrypted_key, api_keys.proxy_encrypted, client_profiles.encrypted_key, and settings.fetch_relay_token). Meanwhile, initDb() calls probeStoredSecrets(), which queries only a single row of api_keys.encrypted_key, causing startup diagnostics, /livez, and /api/health to report the key store as decryptable while omitted tables fail AES-GCM decryption (or, for x_gateway_config.outbound_proxy and proxy pools, fall back to raw ciphertext strings or empty proxy URLs).
claimed_root_cause: ENCRYPTION_GROUPS in server/src/scripts/rotate-encryption-key.ts:121-126 enumerates only api_keys.encrypted_key, api_keys.proxy_encrypted, client_profiles.encrypted_key, and settings.fetch_relay_token instead of rotating all encrypt() and encryptProxyUrl() consumers across x_gateway_keys, x_gateway_proxy_pool, x_gateway_config.outbound_proxy, custom_ai_mcp_servers, custom_ai_approvals, custom_ai_guard_events, and x_support_* tables and archive envelopes; additionally, probeStoredSecrets() in server/src/lib/crypto.ts:231-247 checks only one api_keys row.

applyRotation() atomically writes updated ciphertexts solely for the matched ENCRYPTION_GROUPS rows and main() exits 0, instructing the operator to activate the new ENCRYPTION_KEY and restart.
At server startup under the new ENCRYPTION_KEY, initDb() stores the result of probeStoredSecrets(db) in keyStoreDecryptable without inspecting non-api_keys encrypted tables.

probeStoredSecrets() queries only SELECT encrypted_key AS encrypted, iv, auth_tag FROM api_keys WHERE length(encrypted_key) > 0 LIMIT 1 and returns true (or null if api_keys is empty) despite stale-key ciphertexts in other tables.

Omitted ciphertexts (such as x_support_tenants.secret_encrypted and x_support_db_sources.token_encrypted read by secret(), plus x_gateway_keys, x_gateway_proxy_pool, x_gateway_config, custom_ai_*, and other x_support_* stores) remain encrypted under the old ENCRYPTION_KEY and fail AES-256-GCM decryption under the new key.

title: Weak EXCLUDED_STATEMENT_RE SQL filter and raw db.exec(sql) in restoreBackup allow overwriting excluded account/session tables
description: Database dumps intentionally exclude users, sessions, url_tokens, and registration_requests so backups neither leak dashboard credentials nor allow restore_backups holders or externally edited/supplied dumps to resurrect accounts, replace sessions, or escalate to primary admin. However, restoreBackup() trusts unauthenticated comment headers (parseHeader) and checks dump SQL only with a narrow regex (EXCLUDED_STATEMENT_RE) before executing the full SQL script via db.exec(sql) with foreign_keys disabled, allowing trivial SQLite syntax variants to bypass the guard. Because routes/backups.ts has no .sql upload route and createBackup escapes dumped rows, reachability depends on an external/shared-storage writer, symlinked/unhardened backup path, or operator restoration of an external dump file.
claimed_root_cause: EXCLUDED_STATEMENT_RE in server/src/services/backups.ts:471-474 only matches bare INSERT INTO, DELETE FROM, UPDATE, or DROP TABLE followed by whitespace and an optional double-quoted bare table name, while parseHeader (lines 231-245) trusts unauthenticated SQL comments and backupFilePath (lines 436-445) checks only lexical path containment. SQLite syntax variants such as REPLACE INTO users, INSERT OR REPLACE INTO users, INSERT INTO main.users, INSERT INTO [users], INSERT INTO `users`, DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users, ALTER TABLE users, UPDATE OR REPLACE users, or inline comments (INSERT /*x*/ INTO users) bypass the check and execute in db.exec(sql) at line 550 with PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF (line 538).

trace.description: Authenticated user holding restore_backups (without manage_users or edit_user_roles) triggers POST /api/backups/:id/restore -> restoreBackup(getDb(), id) at line 119.

Reads the backups row (line 483), resolves backupFilePath (line 484, lexical isInside check only), reads the .sql file contents (line 489), and validates unauthenticated comment headers via parseHeader (line 490).

Evaluates header.tables.find(isExcludedTable) and EXCLUDED_STATEMENT_RE.test(sql) (defined at lines 471-474); variants such as INSERT OR REPLACE INTO users, REPLACE INTO users, INSERT INTO main.users, INSERT INTO [users], INSERT INTO `users`, DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users, ALTER TABLE users, or INSERT /*x*/ INTO users return false and pass.

Executes the entire SQL script directly via db.exec(sql) inside db.transaction() after disabling PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF (line 538), allowing modification of excluded users, sessions, url_tokens, and registration_requests tables.

evidence.description: EXCLUDED_TABLES defines users, sessions, url_tokens, and registration_requests as excluded from backup and restore.
parseHeader reads unauthenticated SQL comments (-- format, -- schema, -- key-fingerprint, -- tables) with no HMAC or signature check.
createBackup writes dumps with mode 0o600, calls restrictToOwner(filepath) without checking its boolean return value (line 319), and inserts the backups row (line 323).
backupFilePath checks only lexical isInside(root, candidate) without fs.realpathSync symlink resolution.

EXCLUDED_STATEMENT_RE (lines 471-474) fails to match REPLACE INTO, INSERT OR REPLACE INTO, schema-qualified names (main.users), bracket/backtick identifiers ([users], `users`), DROP TABLE IF EXISTS, ALTER TABLE, UPDATE OR REPLACE, or inline SQL comments.
restoreBackup sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF before running db.exec(sql) inside a transaction at line 550.
PUT /api/backups/schedule lets schedule_backups holders redirect backupPath to any subdirectory under dataDir(db) via assertBackupPathAllowed (line 70).
POST /api/backups only calls createBackup (which filters tables via isBackupableTable and escapes values via sqliteEscape); backupsRouter exposes no .sql upload endpoint.
PERMISSION_GATES gates /api/backups behind manage_backups via installGate and requireActionPermission.
Maps PUT /api/backups/schedule to schedule_backups (line 55) and POST /api/backups/:id/restore to restore_backups (line 56), separate from edit_user_roles (line 36).
shouldHardenDataDir leaves pre-existing non-default FREEAPI_DB_PATH directories unhardened unless FREEAPI_DB_DIR_HARDENING=1 is set.

blockers: Platform Blocker on Windows host (lacks isolated loopback namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only toolchain mounts, and POSIX O_NOFOLLOW promotion) prevents executing restoreBackup against a dummy SQLite fixture inside an OS-enforced sandbox.

server/src/routes/backups.ts exposes no .sql upload endpoint and backups rows are inserted only by createBackup (server/src/services/backups.ts:323) with sqliteEscape (lines 251-258) and isBackupableTable (lines 94-96), so exploitation requires an external/shared-storage writer, symlinked or unhardened backupPath/dataDir(db), or an operator/restore_backups user restoring an externally supplied or edited .sql file linked to a backups row.

validation_plan.local: Inside an OS-enforced sandbox with a temporary SQLite database and isolated directory, seed a dummy non-primary user and a dummy backups row pointing to a test .sql dump with matching schema and key-fingerprint headers plus 'INSERT OR REPLACE INTO users ...' and 'INSERT INTO [users] ...', run restoreBackup(db, id), and verify EXCLUDED_STATEMENT_RE fails to reject it and the dummy users row is overwritten.
validation_plan.deployment: Audit the deployment's dataDir(db) and configured backup_schedule.backupPath directories (including Turso deployments where only .sql dumps reside locally, shared Docker volumes, CIFS/NFS mounts, or custom FREEAPI_DB_PATH directories where restrictToOwner/restrictDirToOwner may fail silently) to verify whether any non-primary-admin principal, sidecar, cloud sync, or operator workflow can place, symlink, or modify .sql files restored via POST /api/backups/:id/restore.

title: Docker Compose autoupdate profile passes empty WATCHTOWER_TOKEN fallback to Docker-socket Watchtower sidecar
description: In `docker-compose.yml`, the opt-in `autoupdate` profile runs `nickfedor/watchtower:1.22.3` with `/var/run/docker.sock` mounted and `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS: update`, interpolating `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN: ${WATCHTOWER_TOKEN:-}`. When `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` is unset or empty (as in `.env.example` and the `.env` quickstart in `docs/en/install/01-install.md`), Compose passes an empty string rather than failing closed (`:?`). Source-visible containment limits direct exposure: `watchtower` is behind `profiles: ["autoupdate"]`, publishes no host `ports`, restricts updates via `WATCHTOWER_LABEL_ENABLE: "true"` and `WATCHTOWER_SCOPE: freellmapi`, and `freellmapi` disables `POST /api/update/apply` (`409 not_configured`, also gated by `requireAuth` and `manage_updates`) when `FREELLMAPI_SELF_UPDATE_TOKEN` is empty. However, whether `nickfedor/watchtower:1.22.3` fails closed or serves `/v1/update` unauthenticated on the Compose network (reachable by co-located containers or `manage_key_models` custom-provider probes when `FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS` is unset) when `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=""` cannot be verified offline from repository source.
claimed_root_cause: Docker Compose environment interpolation uses `${WATCHTOWER_TOKEN:-}` (empty-string fallback) instead of fail-closed `${WATCHTOWER_TOKEN:?...}` for `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN` on the Docker-socket-mounted `watchtower` sidecar.

trace.description: WATCHTOWER_TOKEN is commented out (`# WATCHTOWER_TOKEN=`) by default in the env template, matching the Compose quickstart in `docs/en/install/01-install.md` which creates `.env` without `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN`.
WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN uses `${WATCHTOWER_TOKEN:-}`, expanding an unset or empty WATCHTOWER_TOKEN to `""` instead of aborting startup with `:?`.

With `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS: update` enabled and `/var/run/docker.sock` mounted, Watchtower runs and listens on internal Compose address `http://watchtower:8080/v1/update` with an empty `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN` when `--profile autoupdate` is started.

evidence.description: Pinned sidecar image `nickfedor/watchtower:1.22.3` gated behind opt-in `profiles: ["autoupdate"]` (line 58) with no published host `ports`.
Enables `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS: update` alongside `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN: ${WATCHTOWER_TOKEN:-}` (line 61).

Mounts `/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock` while restricting targets via `WATCHTOWER_LABEL_ENABLE: "true"` (line 62) and `WATCHTOWER_SCOPE: freellmapi` (line 63) to match `freellmapi` labels (lines 20-21).

`freellmapi` checks `Boolean(selfUpdateUrl && selfUpdateToken)` before enabling `POST /api/update/apply` (line 666, behind `requireAuth` in `server/src/app.ts:314` and the `manage_settings` -> `manage_updates` permission gate in `server/src/custom/register.ts:102` and `server/src/custom/permission-actions.ts:124`), so it returns 409 when `FREELLMAPI_SELF_UPDATE_TOKEN` (`docker-compose.yml:15`) is empty.
Docker Compose quickstart generates `.env` with only `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `PORT`, leaving `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` unset unless explicitly added per line 250.

`POST /api/keys/custom/discover-models` (requiring `manage_key_models`, without `manage_settings`) calls `assessProviderUrl` (line 1106 / `server/src/lib/url-guard.ts:263`), which allows private Compose network targets unless `FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS` is set.

blockers: The pinned third-party `nickfedor/watchtower:1.22.3` image source/binary is not in this repository and Docker cannot be executed on this offline Windows host without the required OS-enforced sandbox, so whether Watchtower refuses to start, rejects requests with 401, or serves `/v1/update` unauthenticated on GET/POST when `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=""` is unverified.

Because `watchtower` publishes no host ports and `freellmapi` disables `/api/update/apply` when `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` is empty, reachability depends on owner-observed deployment state: whether `--profile autoupdate` is enabled with `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` unset/empty in `.env`, whether other containers/overlays share the Compose network with `watchtower:8080`, and whether `FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS` is unset alongside delegated `manage_keys` accounts.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated Linux/Docker sandbox with no external network and a dummy label-matched container, run `docker compose --profile autoupdate config` with `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` unset and start `nickfedor/watchtower:1.22.3` with `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_ENDPOINTS=update` and `WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN=""` to observe startup behavior and HTTP GET/POST responses from `http://watchtower:8080/v1/update` without a Bearer token and with an empty Bearer token.
validation_plan.deployment: Inspect the deployed Compose project to verify whether `--profile autoupdate` is active (`docker compose ps`), check whether `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` is non-empty in `.env` and rendered in `docker compose --profile autoupdate config`, verify whether any additional containers share the Compose network with `watchtower:8080`, and verify whether `FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS=true` is configured if delegated `manage_keys` users exist.

title: Windows dev-bootstrap script writes ENCRYPTION_KEY to .env without NTFS owner-only ACL restriction
description: Unlike scripts/dev-bootstrap.sh (which sets umask 077 before creating .env), scripts/dev-bootstrap.ps1 generates a 32-byte AES-256-GCM ENCRYPTION_KEY and writes .env using Set-Content without applying NTFS owner-only ACL hardening via icacls.exe. On server startup, server/src/env.ts loads .env and server/src/lib/crypto.ts uses ENCRYPTION_KEY as the primary master encryption key (superseding the ACL-restricted .encryption-key dev fallback), while server/src/db/index.ts only restricts server/data and freeapi.db rather than the repository root or .env. When bootstrapped in a Windows directory outside an isolated user profile (such as a drive-root checkout inheriting BUILTIN\Users or Authenticated Users ACEs), other non-admin local Windows accounts or AppContainers can read ENCRYPTION_KEY from .env, undermining the NTFS ACL protections in server/src/lib/file-permissions.ts.
claimed_root_cause: scripts/dev-bootstrap.ps1 relies on default inherited NTFS parent-directory ACLs when creating .env with Set-Content, rather than stripping inherited ACEs and restricting permissions to owner, SYSTEM, and Administrators as implemented in server/src/lib/file-permissions.ts (icacls.exe /inheritance:r) and matched by umask 077 in scripts/dev-bootstrap.sh.

When .env does not exist (line 80), generates a 64-character hex 32-byte ENCRYPTION_KEY via Node crypto.randomBytes(32).
Creates .env containing ENCRYPTION_KEY via Set-Content -LiteralPath $envFile -Encoding ascii without stripping inherited NTFS directory ACEs.

evidence.description: Set-Content -LiteralPath $envFile -Encoding ascii writes ENCRYPTION_KEY to .env with inherited directory NTFS ACLs and no icacls.exe hardening.
POSIX counterpart explicitly sets umask 077 before writing ENCRYPTION_KEY to .env on line 73.

Invokes System32\icacls.exe with /inheritance:r and owner/SYSTEM/Administrators grants to restrict sensitive files (.encryption-key, freeapi.db, backups) on Windows.
Loads .env from the repository root on server startup when FREEAPI_ENV_PATH is unset.
Reads process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY as the primary AES-256-GCM master encryption key, whereas the .encryption-key fallback is ACL-restricted via restrictToOwner (lines 79-83).
Validates .env content and preservation for scripts/dev-bootstrap.ps1 without asserting NTFS ACL restriction.

blockers: Target code execution is omitted on this Windows host because the OS-enforced execution sandbox (isolated network namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only target/tool mounts, scratch-only writes, resource caps, and POSIX O_NOFOLLOW promotion) is unavailable.

Whether non-owner local Windows principals (such as BUILTIN\Users, Authenticated Users, or AppContainers) can read ENCRYPTION_KEY from .env depends on the inherited NTFS ACL of the host directory where the repository is cloned (e.g., drive-root or shared directory vs. private %USERPROFILE%) and whether the host has multiple local users or sandboxed workloads.

title: Electron desktop window permits cross-port 127.0.0.1 navigation and HTTP redirects while exposing admin session and OS bridges via preload
description: `desktop/src/main.ts` filters navigation only via `isExternal(url)`, which checks `(u.protocol === 'http:' || u.protocol === 'https:') && u.hostname !== '127.0.0.1'` without checking the server's bound `resolvedPort` or non-HTTP schemes, and registers no `will-redirect` listener. Combined with `desktop/src/window.ts` attaching `preload.cjs` (`sandbox: false`) and `ipcMain` handlers performing no `event.senderFrame` origin check, any navigation to another local service on `127.0.0.1:<otherPort>` or any server-side 3xx redirect to a remote origin runs `desktop/src/preload.ts`, writing `--freeapi-token` into that origin's `localStorage` and exposing `__FREEAPI_SESSION__` (minting fresh primary-admin session tokens), `__FREEAPI_LOGIN_ITEM__`, and `__FREEAPI_UPDATER__`.
claimed_root_cause: Navigation filtering checks only `hostname !== '127.0.0.1'` on `will-navigate`/`window-open` without pinning `port === resolvedPort`, handling `will-redirect`, or verifying `event.senderFrame` origin on `ipcMain` handlers.

trace.description: Creates BrowserWindow with preload.cjs (line 33), sandbox: false (line 35), additionalArguments carrying --freeapi-token (line 39), and loads http://127.0.0.1:${port} (line 43).
isExternal returns false for http(s)://127.0.0.1:<anyPort> and non-http(s) URLs in will-navigate (lines 98-103), with no will-redirect handler registered.
Writes --freeapi-token into window.localStorage and exposes __FREEAPI_SESSION__ (line 31), __FREEAPI_LOGIN_ITEM__ (line 40), and __FREEAPI_UPDATER__ (line 60) to the top-level document.
Mints a fresh primary-admin desktopSessionToken via ensureSessionToken() without checking event.senderFrame.

evidence.description: openDashboard loads only the trusted embedded server URL http://127.0.0.1:${port} and leaves nodeIntegrationInSubFrames unset (default false) at lines 32-40.

setWindowOpenHandler unconditionally returns { action: 'deny' } (line 96), and isExternal (line 88) returns false for 127.0.0.1 and non-http(s) URLs, blocking popups and target="_blank" links without calling shell.openExternal or navigating dashboardWindow.
ipcMain.handle('freeapi:session-token') and sibling IPC handlers (lines 107-171) do not check event.senderFrame, and will-redirect is not registered alongside will-navigate (lines 98-103).
Unconditionally sets freellmapi_dashboard_token in window.localStorage and exposes __FREEAPI_SESSION__ (line 31), __FREEAPI_LOGIN_ITEM__ (line 40), and __FREEAPI_UPDATER__ (line 60).

Markdown links force target="_blank", and client/src/custom/x-gateway/PlaygroundMessage.tsx (line 604) similarly forces target="_blank" on all rendered <a> elements while parseHtmlFragment (lines 247-345) blocks <iframe>, <form>, <meta>, and <script>.

ARTIFACT_SANDBOX ('allow-scripts allow-forms allow-modals allow-popups allow-pointer-lock') omits allow-top-navigation and allow-same-origin for Playground srcDoc iframes (artifact-panel.tsx:170, PlaygroundMessage.tsx:523).

Helmet CSP restricts scripts, forms, and base URI to 'self' (lines 155-168), and server/src/routes/external-auth.ts (lines 55, 59) is the only res.redirect route, redirecting only to operator-configured PUBLIC_APP_URL.

reason: Refuted by source controls: while desktop/src/main.ts lacks port pinning in isExternal (line 88), a will-redirect listener (lines 98-103), and event.senderFrame checks on ipcMain handlers (lines 107-171), the candidate lacks any real lower-trust entrypoint or reachable navigation/redirect trigger. First, openDashboard (desktop/src/window.ts:43) loads only the trusted embedded server at http://127.0.0.1:${resolvedPort}, and desktop/src/popover.ts:65 loads only static desktop/renderer/popover.html using preload-popover.cjs and .textContent. Second, all external and model/user-rendered <a> links across client/src/ (including client/src/components/markdown.tsx:87-90, client/src/custom/x-gateway/PlaygroundMessage.tsx:602-605, and client/src/components/playground/search-sources.tsx:23-26) force target="_blank" (and PlaygroundMessage's parseHtmlFragment excludes <iframe>, <form>, <meta>, and <script>), routing clicks and window.open calls through setWindowOpenHandler (desktop/src/main.ts:94-97), which unconditionally returns { action: 'deny' } and does not call shell.openExternal for 127.0.0.1 or non-http(s) URLs. Third, Playground HTML/SVG artifact previews run inside <iframe sandbox={ARTIFACT_SANDBOX} srcDoc={...}> (client/src/components/playground/artifact-panel.tsx:170, PlaygroundMessage.tsx:523), where ARTIFACT_SANDBOX (client/src/lib/artifacts.ts:76) omits allow-top-navigation, allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation, and allow-same-origin, and desktop/src/window.ts:32-40 leaves nodeIntegrationInSubFrames disabled (default false) so preload.cjs does not load in subframes. Fourth, the only client location assignment (client/src/custom/GoogleSignIn.tsx:53-55) strictly pins https://accounts.google.com (intercepted by isExternal in will-navigate), server/src/app.ts:152-171 enforces Helmet CSP (default-src 'self', script-src 'self', form-action 'self', base-uri 'self'), and no embedded server route provides an untrusted 3xx redirect (server/src/routes/external-auth.ts:55,59 redirects only to operator-configured PUBLIC_APP_URL, unset in packaged desktop builds). Reaching will-navigate to 127.0.0.1:<otherPort> or a 3xx redirect would already require arbitrary top-level script/navigation control inside the already-privileged 127.0.0.1:${resolvedPort} origin (which already holds the session token and preload bridges), while local same-host callers can already obtain a desktopSessionToken via POST /api/auth/desktop-session (server/src/routes/auth.ts:184-190).

title: Desktop primary-admin session token is passed via Electron renderer additionalArguments (OS command line)
description: desktop/src/main.ts obtains a 30-day primary-admin session token via ensureSessionToken() (desktopSessionToken() in server/src/services/auth.ts, for desktop@localhost or the lowest-id user) and passes it to openDashboard(port, sessionToken), where desktop/src/window.ts places `--freeapi-token=${token}` into BrowserWindow webPreferences.additionalArguments. Electron forwards additionalArguments to the spawned renderer child process (consumed via process.argv in desktop/src/preload.ts). On multi-user systems where freeapi.db and .encryption-key are explicitly restricted to the owner via file-permissions.ts (0600 on POSIX, owner/SYSTEM/Administrators ACL on Windows), exposing the live bearer token in renderer OS process arguments can disclose the session credential to other local OS accounts via process listings (e.g., ps or /proc/<pid>/cmdline on Linux without hidepid, or ps on macOS; standard non-admin Windows accounts lack cross-user process command-line read privileges). Note that on running desktop instances (FREEAPI_DESKTOP=1), POST /api/auth/desktop-session in server/src/routes/auth.ts also allows unauthenticated loopback requests without OS-user verification, representing a separate local boundary weakness rather than a control that prevents argv disclosure.
claimed_root_cause: The desktop shell transports a live authentication bearer token across the main-to-renderer boundary via BrowserWindow webPreferences.additionalArguments (OS process CLI arguments) instead of origin-verified Chromium IPC.

trace.description: Calls ensureSessionToken() (desktopSessionToken()) to mint a 30-day primary-admin sessionToken for desktop@localhost (or the lowest-id user).
Passes sessionToken into openDashboard(port, sessionToken) on launch (also invoked via buildTray at lines 310-312 / desktop/src/tray.ts:44,53 and ipcMain handler freeapi:open-dashboard at line 152).

Places --freeapi-token=${token} in BrowserWindow webPreferences.additionalArguments when creating the dashboard window at line 25, spawning the renderer child process with the live bearer token in its process arguments.

evidence.description: Sets additionalArguments: [`--freeapi-token=${token}`, `--freeapi-version=${app.getVersion()}`] inside BrowserWindow webPreferences.
Reads process.argv.find((a) => a.startsWith('--freeapi-token=')) in the renderer preload and seeds window.localStorage at line 12.
desktopSessionToken() ensures the hidden machine user (desktop@localhost, primary admin when userCount() === 0) exists and returns a 30-day session token from createSession(first.id).

restrictDbFilePermissions() restricts freeapi.db and its -wal/-shm sidecars to owner (0600 on POSIX, owner/SYSTEM/Administrators ACL on Windows), matching .encryption-key hardening in server/src/lib/crypto.ts:75-84.

ipcMain.handle('freeapi:session-token', ...) already supplies ensureSessionToken() over Chromium IPC for __FREEAPI_SESSION__ (desktop/src/preload.ts:31), though without event.senderFrame origin verification.
Context on desktop loopback posture: POST /api/auth/desktop-session separately mints desktopSessionToken() for loopback callers when FREEAPI_DESKTOP=1 without OS-user peer verification.

blockers: OS-enforced execution sandbox controls (isolated loopback namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only mounts, scratch-only writes, resource limits, POSIX O_NOFOLLOW) are unavailable on this Windows host, and desktop/node_modules (including electron@^38.8.6) is not installed, preventing live Electron renderer launch and process-table inspection.

Actual cross-account OS command-line disclosure depends on platform-specific Electron/Chromium renderer spawning (e.g., Linux Zygote vs --no-zygote command-line rewriting in /proc/<pid>/cmdline) and OS host policy (Linux /proc hidepid mount option, macOS ps visibility, and Windows cross-user PEB/WMI access controls).

validation_plan.local: In an isolated test environment with desktop dependencies installed (desktop/node_modules) and a disposable dummy userData/APPDATA directory, build the desktop bundles (npm --prefix desktop run build:all), launch Electron against the dummy directory so openDashboard() spawns the dashboard BrowserWindow, and inspect the renderer child process command line (e.g., /proc/<renderer-pid>/cmdline on Linux or ps -p <renderer-pid> -ww -o command= on macOS) from the same and a second unprivileged dummy OS account to confirm whether --freeapi-token= appears in OS-visible argv.
validation_plan.deployment: Inspect target multi-user host process-visibility policy (such as Linux /proc hidepid=1/2 mount options and macOS multi-user ps output) while the desktop dashboard window is open, verify whether unprivileged local OS accounts can read --freeapi-token= from the Electron renderer command line, and remediate by removing --freeapi-token= from desktop/src/window.ts additionalArguments in favor of origin-verified Chromium IPC (validating event.senderFrame URL origin against http://127.0.0.1:<resolvedPort> in freeapi:session-token) alongside hardening desktop loopback authentication.

title: GoogleProvider fetches inference-caller image_url targets on loopback and private networks by default
description: Lower-trust inference callers (sk-flm- member keys and sk-cp- client-profile keys via /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, or /v1/responses, and flmurl_ URL tokens via /v1/t/:token/chat/completions or /v1/t/:token/responses) routing to GoogleProvider can supply http(s) image_url values that fetchImageChecked validates via assessProviderUrl without { blockPrivate: true }. When FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS is unset or not enabled (the default), assessProviderUrl permits loopback (127.0.0.0/8, localhost, ::1, 0.0.0.0) and RFC1918/CGNAT/ULA private-network addresses, and shouldBypassProxy in proxy.ts routes loopback and private-literal/localhost targets directly via fetch() (unless PROXY_REQUIRED_PLATFORMS includes google), enabling server-side HTTP GET requests against localhost/LAN endpoints and forwarding up to 8 MB of fetched content as base64 inlineData in outbound Gemini API calls.
claimed_root_cause: server/src/providers/google.ts:360 calls assessProviderUrl(url) without { blockPrivate: true }, inheriting blockPrivateEnabled() (server/src/lib/url-guard.ts:207-209, 254), which defaults to false when FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS is unset so that admin-configured custom providers can reach local inference servers, thereby permitting untrusted inference-caller image_url inputs to target loopback and private LAN addresses.

trace.description: Lower-trust inference caller (sk-flm- member key, sk-cp- client-profile key, or flmurl_ URL token via server/src/routes/url-tokens.ts:32) passes requireInferenceAuth (1897) and chatCompletionSchema (794, 1901; contentBlockSchema at 696) with a user message containing an http(s) image_url block; normalizeMessageImages (2074) leaves http(s) URLs untouched and routeRequest (2589) dispatches vision requests to GoogleProvider.chatCompletion (3145) or streamChatCompletion (2749).

Calls toGeminiContents(messages) (also at line 682 in streamChatCompletion), which walks user turns via userContentToParts (410-429, 510) and passes each http(s) image_url to imageUrlToInlineData -> fetchImageChecked (391-393, 421).

Calls assessProviderUrl(url) without { blockPrivate: true }, so blockPrivate defaults to blockPrivateEnabled() (server/src/lib/url-guard.ts:208, 254) which is false when FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS is unset, allowing loopback and RFC1918/CGNAT/ULA private addresses.

Calls proxyFetch(url, { signal, redirect: 'manual' }, 'google', 'image', 30_000) to fetch the image target (and reads up to MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 8 MB into base64 inlineData at lines 397-400 for the Gemini request at line 620).

Because shouldBypassProxy (519) returns true for loopback and private hostnames unless FREEAPI_PROXY_LOCAL_DESTINATIONS=true, dispatchFetch bypasses any configured outbound proxy and issues a direct fetch(url, init) to the internal target (unless PROXY_REQUIRED_PLATFORMS includes google, which throws at 969-970).

evidence.description: requireInferenceAuth admits sk-flm- member keys and sk-cp- client-profile keys (resolved via server/src/lib/system-prompt.ts:59-83), while chatCompletionSchema (696, 794, 1901) accepts arbitrary image_url objects and normalizeMessageImages (2074) only processes data: URLs.

imageBlockToUrl also forwards Anthropic image blocks with source.type === 'url' as image_url blocks (348) to route.provider.chatCompletion (779), and server/src/routes/responses.ts:294 forwards Responses input_image URLs likewise (1612).
fetchImageChecked runs assessProviderUrl(url) without { blockPrivate: true } on caller-supplied http(s) image_url values and redirect targets.
imageUrlToInlineData buffers up to MAX_IMAGE_BYTES (8 MB, 335, 398) from the fetched response and attaches base64 inlineData (400) to the outbound Gemini API body (620, 701).

assessProviderUrl defaults blockPrivate to blockPrivateEnabled() (207-209), allowing loopback and RFC1918/ULA/CGNAT addresses whenever FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS is unset (documented at lines 20-23).

shouldBypassProxy returns true for loopback and private hostnames when FREEAPI_PROXY_LOCAL_DESTINATIONS is unset, causing dispatchFetch (968-972) to issue a direct fetch() rather than routing through a configured outbound proxy unless PROXY_REQUIRED_PLATFORMS includes google.

Comparable baseline: X-Gateway's assertFetchTarget (2127-2145) explicitly passes { blockPrivate: true } to assessProviderUrl (2140), and server/src/custom/x-gateway/playground-router.ts:11 restricts image_url strictly to data:image/...;base64,... URLs.

blockers: Execution sandbox unavailable on Windows host (lacks isolated loopback namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only toolchain mounts, and POSIX O_NOFOLLOW descriptor-walk promotion), preventing safe runtime reproduction against an isolated loopback HTTP image fixture.

Deployment configuration is unknown from source alone: whether FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS is set to 1/true/yes, whether an enabled healthy google provider key and vision model are configured and reachable to lower-trust callers (sk-flm-, sk-cp- whose allowed_models are empty or include google models, or flmurl_ tokens), and whether PROXY_REQUIRED_PLATFORMS includes google.

Send a POST /v1/chat/completions request authenticated with the dummy key containing an image_url pointing to the 127.0.0.1 fixture URL and verify the GET request arrives directly at the loopback server and its base64 bytes appear as inlineData in the mocked Gemini payload.

title: normalizeMessageImages invokes sharp without limitInputPixels and re-decodes full-resolution buffers for stats()
description: Authenticated inference endpoints (including POST /v1/chat/completions, POST /v1/messages, POST /v1/responses, and inbound Gemini/Ollama chat routes, gated to unified-key, sk-flm- member, sk-cp- client-profile, URL-token, or open-loopback Ollama callers) invoke normalizeMessageImages before vision-model availability and token-budget checks. candidateOf only skips sub-threshold JPEG and WebP inputs, so inline PNG, SVG, TIFF, GIF, BMP, and AVIF data URLs of any byte size pass to sharp(buffer) with no explicit limitInputPixels cap (relying on sharp 0.35.3's default 268,402,689-pixel limit, unlike the 16 MP cap in media adapters) and invoke sharp(buffer).stats() on a second unresized instance with VIPS_ACCESS_RANDOM when meta.hasAlpha is true. Inside a 25 MB request (or 256 KiB unauth body threshold after auth), small compressed PNG/SVG payloads near ~268 MP can trigger large native libvips raster allocations per image.
claimed_root_cause: server/src/lib/image-normalize.ts:190-196 only skips sub-threshold image/jpeg and image/webp inputs; normalizeDataUrl calls sharp(buffer) at line 213 without an explicit limitInputPixels cap (contrast server/src/services/media.ts:663 and server/src/services/media-varosity.ts:125 at 16 MP), and calls sharp(buffer).stats() at line 241 on the full unresized buffer when meta.hasAlpha is true across every queued image block in work at lines 306-313.

trace.description: Accepts authenticated chat completion requests (unified, sk-flm-, sk-cp-, or /v1/t/:token callers up to the 25 MB JSON body limit configured at server/src/lib/config.ts:20 and server/src/app.ts:223-226).
Calls normalizeMessageImages(messages) on parsed chat messages before checking hasEnabledVisionModel() (line 2090) or applyTokenBudget() (line 2134).
Only skips images below thresholdBytes when alreadyCompact is true (image/jpeg or image/webp at line 190), forwarding any size base64 image/png, image/svg+xml, image/tiff, or image/gif data URL.
Constructs sharp(buffer) without limitInputPixels, falling back to sharp 0.35.3's default 268,402,689-pixel (0x3FFF^2) ceiling.

Creates a second uncapped sharp(buffer) instance on the unresized buffer and awaits .stats() (random-access multi-pass evaluation) whenever meta.hasAlpha is true across every slot in work (lines 306-313), before pipeline encode (lines 247-254).

evidence.description: Documents decoding PNG, TIFF, GIF, BMP, AVIF, and SVG rasterized at native size.
Skips decode only when rawBytes < opts.thresholdBytes and alreadyCompact (JPEG/WebP), letting small PNG/SVG/TIFF/GIF payloads enter sharp.
Calls sharp(buffer) without limitInputPixels (unlike server/src/services/media.ts:663 and server/src/services/media-varosity.ts:125, which enforce 16 * 1024 * 1024).
Calls sharp(buffer).stats() on the unresized original buffer when meta.hasAlpha is true rather than on the downscaled pipeline.
Comments that target deployments include small hosts such as a Raspberry Pi or 512 MB VPS, alongside the 25 MB default request body limit at line 20.
Baseline in the same codebase explicitly passes limitInputPixels: 16 * 1024 * 1024 to sharp().
Invokes normalizeMessageImages before vision-model and token-budget rejections (same pattern at anthropic.ts:539, responses.ts:797, and inbound-chat.ts:177).

title: POST /api/auth/register creates the user before claiming the invite and ignores claimInviteCode() returning false
description: In POST /api/auth/register (server/src/custom/auth.ts:103-146), validateInviteCode(inviteCode) performs a non-locking read check (line 115) outside any transaction, createUser(email, password, 'member') then inserts and commits the user row (line 130) without a transaction, and claimInviteCode(inviteCode) is called afterward (line 141) while discarding its boolean return value. Although synchronous execution inside a single Node.js process serializes concurrent requests on the main thread, claimInviteCode() can still return false after validateInviteCode() passed in two source-verified scenarios: (1) wall-clock expiry boundary/drift, because validateInviteCode allows row.expires_at_ms === Date.now() (< at server/src/services/invites.ts:152) whereas claimInviteCode requires expires_at_ms > ? at line 176 after createUser runs synchronous crypto.scryptSync() (server/src/lib/password.ts:10) and four synchronous DB queries (server/src/services/auth.ts:49-75); and (2) multi-process/shared-DB concurrency (such as rolling deploys against Turso noted at server/src/db/turso.ts:142) or Turso's 3-second SELECT result cache at depth === 0 (server/src/db/turso.ts:80, 325), where another writer exhausts or revokes the invite between validateInviteCode and claimInviteCode. Because claimInviteCode returning false is ignored and createUser already committed, lines 143-145 unconditionally mint a personal sk-flm- API key, issue a 30-day session token, and respond HTTP 201. By contrast, finishGoogleLogin (server/src/services/google-auth.ts:187, 229-233) wraps user creation, invite claiming, and key minting in db.transaction() and aborts if claimInviteCode returns false.
claimed_root_cause: POST /api/auth/register executes validateInviteCode and createUser outside a transaction with claimInviteCode and fails to inspect or roll back on claimInviteCode() returning false.

trace.description: Unauthenticated HTTP handler for POST /api/auth/register (mounted at /api/auth in server/src/custom/register.ts:298 below adminRateLimiter in server/src/app.ts:258), subject only to a 20-per-15-min IP bucket (line 104) and Zod body validation (line 108).

Calls validateInviteCode(inviteCode) as an unlocked pre-flight SELECT outside any transaction, accepting expires_at_ms === Date.now() (< check at server/src/services/invites.ts:152) and, on Turso at depth === 0, potentially reading the 3-second SELECT cache (server/src/db/turso.ts:80, 325).

Calls createUser(email, password, 'member') outside any transaction, committing the member user row after synchronous crypto.scryptSync hashing (server/src/lib/password.ts:10) and four synchronous DB operations (server/src/services/auth.ts:49-75) during which Date.now() advances and external DB writers can mutate invite_codes.

Calls claimInviteCode(inviteCode) after user creation and discards its boolean return value (result.changes > 0 at server/src/services/invites.ts:179), ignoring false when the invite has expired (> at invites.ts:176), been revoked, or reached max_uses.

title: POST /api/keys/custom bypasses guardKeyAddition via keyId references and mixed-case paths under add_keys
description: permissionForAction lowercases req.originalUrl and gates POST /api/keys/custom on add_keys while requiring edit_keys for PATCH /api/keys/:id (groupLabel/key edits) and manage_key_models for model registration. Although registerCustomRoutes mounts guardKeyAddition before keysRouter to enforce manage_key_models when model/models are present and edit_keys when modifying an existing custom baseUrl (including groupLabel or overwriting 'no-key' placeholders), guardKeyAddition fails open on two paths: (1) for lowercase POST /api/keys/custom in the credential-only branch, guardKeyAddition returns next() at line 34 whenever baseUrl is omitted in favor of keyId, allowing an add_keys-only principal to resolve the existing endpoint by keyId, overwrite 'no-key' credentials, and update group_label across the entire endpoint key pool via setCustomEndpointGroup without edit_keys; and (2) guardKeyAddition reads req.originalUrl without lowercasing and tests a case-sensitive regex without /i, whereas Express routes case-insensitively by default, so mixed-case POST /api/keys/Custom bypasses guardKeyAddition completely and lets an add_keys-only caller register/re-enable chat, media, and embedding models, overwrite 'no-key' rows or re-enable disabled keys, and mutate group_label without edit_keys or manage_key_models. Unlike the comparable meta-gateway designs noted in the architecture baseline, this arises from mismatched URL normalization and reference-field coverage between permissionForAction, guardKeyAddition, and keysRouter.
claimed_root_cause: permissionForAction grants POST /api/keys/custom on add_keys after lowercasing the path, while guardKeyAddition fails to normalize path case before matching /custom and exits before checking edit_keys whenever baseUrl is omitted in favor of keyId, allowing add_keys-only callers to reach keysRouter.post('/custom') sinks that mutate existing endpoint group_label, overwrite 'no-key' credentials or re-enable disabled keys, and register/update custom models without edit_keys or manage_key_models.

Reads req.originalUrl without lowercasing (line 14) and matches /^\/api\/(keys|embeddings|media|decisions)\/custom$/ without the /i flag (line 26), causing mixed-case POST /api/keys/Custom to return next() at line 27 and skip both manage_key_models (line 30) and edit_keys (lines 31-46).

Even on lowercase POST /api/keys/custom, returns next() at line 34 whenever typeof body.baseUrl !== 'string', skipping the existing-endpoint edit_keys checks (lines 35-46) for credential-only payloads that reference an existing endpoint via keyId.
Express routes /custom case-insensitively (app.ts:113, keys.ts:1389) and calls resolveEndpointRef(parsed.data) (lines 982-1018) to locate an existing custom endpoint row by keyId or baseUrl.

Calls setCustomEndpointGroup (line 1511, and line 1471 in the credential-only branch reachable on lowercase /api/keys/custom via keyId) to update group_label across the existing endpoint's key pool, calls resolveCustomEndpointKey (lines 1470 and 1508, touching/re-enabling existing rows or overwriting 'no-key' placeholders), and calls registerCustomModels/registerCustomMediaModel/registerCustomEmbeddingModel (lines 1508-1547) without edit_keys or manage_key_models.

PATCH /api/keys/:id (which updates groupLabel, label, enabled, and credentials) requires edit_keys.

guardKeyAddition skips existing-endpoint edit_keys checks (lines 35-46) whenever typeof body.baseUrl !== 'string', leaving keyId-referenced requests unguarded.

customProviderSchema allows requests supplying keyId without baseUrl.

Credential-only branch invokes resolveCustomEndpointKey, overwriting 'no-key' sentinel rows in place (custom-endpoint.ts:161-170).
Credential-only branch invokes setCustomEndpointGroup to mutate group_label across the existing endpoint's key pool under add_keys when keyId is used without baseUrl.

title: Unauthenticated Google OAuth login silently links unverified local accounts (including admin) by email and omits sk-xgw- revocation
description: In finishGoogleLogin (server/src/services/google-auth.ts:181-251), when a Google OAuth callback returns an unmapped Google subject, the handler queries SELECT id, email, role FROM users WHERE email = ? using the normalized Google email and inserts a permanent auth_google_identities binding whenever identity.authoritative (@gmail.com or non-empty Workspace hd at lines 143-145) is true and user.id has no existing Google link (lines 204-214). Local account emails stored via POST /api/auth/setup, POST /api/auth/change-email, POST /api/auth/register, and approveRegistrationRequest are never verified for email ownership, and finishGoogleLogin checks neither an authenticated local session nor user.role !== 'admin'. Consequently, an unauthenticated attacker controlling a Google account matching any unlinked local admin or member email can permanently link their Google subject and obtain a dashboard session for that account (leaving admin passwords, sessions, and API keys untouched, and for member takeovers at lines 221-227 revoking only user_api_keys while leaving x_gateway_client_keys sk-xgw- active and users.permissions intact).
claimed_root_cause: finishGoogleLogin trusts unverified local users.email values to perform unauthenticated Google OAuth account linking across both admin and member roles without authenticated session or password confirmation, and member-takeover cleanup omits x_gateway_client_keys revocation.

trace.description: Unauthenticated OAuth callback mounted under /api/auth (server/src/custom/register.ts:300) exchanges the authorization code via exchangeGoogleCode (line 52) and invokes finishGoogleLogin(identity, attempt.inviteCode) (line 53) without requiring an authenticated local session.

When identity.subject is not yet mapped in auth_google_identities (lines 189-196), looks up any existing local account (admin or member) purely by unverified normalized email and gates linking only on identity.authoritative and absence of an existing auth_google_identities row for user.id (lines 206-210).

Inserts (identity.subject, user.id) into auth_google_identities and creates a dashboard session via createSession(user.id) at line 240 (redeemed at POST /api/auth/google/complete); admin takeovers leave existing sessions/passwords/keys intact, and member cleanup at lines 221-227 revokes user_api_keys (line 225) while omitting x_gateway_client_keys (sk-xgw-).

evidence.description: Mounts externalAuthRouter at /api/auth without requireAuth (ahead of requireAuth-gated mounts), leaving /api/auth/google/start, /callback, and /complete reachable without an authenticated local session.

POST /api/auth/setup calls createUser without verifying email ownership; POST /api/auth/change-email (line 289 -> updateEmail at server/src/services/auth.ts:190), POST /api/auth/register (server/src/custom/auth.ts:130), and approveRegistrationRequest (server/src/services/registration-requests.ts:148) likewise persist unverified local emails.

The linking gate checks only !identity.authoritative (@gmail.com or non-empty hd at lines 143-145) and no existing auth_google_identities row for user.id (lines 207-209), permitting unauthenticated takeover of unlinked admin or member accounts with unverified matching emails.
When user.role === 'member', cleanup updates password_hash, deletes sessions, and revokes user_api_keys (lines 221-227), leaving x_gateway_client_keys rows unrevoked and users.permissions unchanged.

validateXGatewayClientKey authenticates sk-xgw- tokens against x_gateway_client_keys checking only !row.revoked (line 220), so a member granted use_x_gateway (checked in server/src/custom/x-gateway/auth.ts:31) retains /thruline/v1 and /v1beta inference access after Google takeover.

blockers: Execution disabled on Windows host (lacks OS-enforced execution sandbox: no isolated loopback namespace, empty allowlisted env, read-only toolchain mounts, or POSIX O_NOFOLLOW descriptor-walk promotion); verification is restricted to read-only source inspection.

Exploitability requires deployment configuration enabling Google OAuth (PUBLIC_APP_URL, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET making getExternalAuthConfig().google non-null) and an unlinked local account whose unverified users.email matches an attacker-controlled Google @gmail.com or Workspace (hd) account (plus Thruline enabled for /thruline/v1 and an active sk-xgw- key for a member holding use_x_gateway for residual key persistence).

validation_plan.local: Inside an OS-enforced sandbox with mocked exchangeGoogleCode/verifyGoogleIdToken (no external network), run a Vitest integration test against an in-memory SQLite DB: (1) create an unlinked local admin via POST /api/auth/setup with an unverified @gmail.com email, execute /api/auth/google/start -> /api/auth/google/callback -> /api/auth/google/complete using a mocked GoogleIdentity for that email, and verify auth_google_identities binds to the admin userId and issues a valid admin session without invalidating prior sessions; (2) repeat with Thruline enabled (setEnabled(true)) and a member granted use_x_gateway holding both sk-flm- and sk-xgw- keys and confirm sk-flm- is revoked while sk-xgw- still authenticates against /thruline/v1.
