title: Output guard /test endpoint permits view_output_guard caller to trigger upstream moderation API calls despite canCallGateway: false
description: POST /api/ai-platform/output-guard/:scopeKind/:scopeId/test is gated by requirePerm('view_output_guard') and accepts an inline policy object and includeExternal boolean. Although the handler passes canCallGateway: false to testPolicy so runJudgeCheck cannot invoke upstream gateway inference, evaluateExternalDetectors calls runModerationCheck -> runModerations(undefined, [text], ...) whenever moderation.enabled is true without checking ctx.canCallGateway === false, allowing a view_output_guard caller to initiate outbound moderation API requests against configured provider keys.
claimed_root_cause: runModerationCheck / evaluateExternalDetectors in output-guard/external.ts omits the canCallGateway === false check that blocks runJudgeCheck when invoked from the view_output_guard /test route.

trace.description: Gates POST /output-guard/:scopeKind/:scopeId/test on exact child permission 'view_output_guard' and parses optional inline policy and includeExternal via testRequestSchema (lines 146-153).
Calls testPolicy(scope, parsed.data, { req, signal: ac.signal, systemPrompt: null, canCallGateway: false }) unconditionally for all callers.

When outputGuard pillar flag is enabled (line 390), req.includeExternal is true, and inline or stored policy.mode !== 'off' has moderation or judge enabled, forwards policy and canCallGateway: ctx.canCallGateway to evaluateExternalDetectors.
Calls runModerationCheck -> runModerations(undefined, [text], ...) (line 92) whenever moderation.enabled is true without checking ctx.canCallGateway.

evidence.description: aiPlatformPermission explicitly maps POST /output-guard/:scopeKind/:scopeId/test to 'view_output_guard'.
Handler passes canCallGateway: false unconditionally for every caller (including primary admin), not only view_output_guard.
runJudgeCheck checks !ctx.req || ctx.canCallGateway === false because it calls callGateway(ctx.req, ...) against /v1/chat/completions.
Inference-side caller names this capability canRunExternalJudge (derived from extractInferenceToken(req)), confirming canCallGateway gates only the loopback judge call.
hasInferenceCapability (mapped to canCallGateway in policy.ts:527) is explicitly documented for external judge calls only.
testPolicy explicitly gates external detector execution on req.includeExternal and isPillarEnabled('outputGuard'), with router.ts:268 as its sole non-test caller.

runModerations uses stored openai/openrouter/nvidia keys against hardcoded MODERATION_MODELS URLs (lines 78-82) with checkMonthlyBudget (line 249) and sanitized/non-secret results, never calling callGateway or using ctx.req.
view_output_guard is explicitly defined as 'View output guard policies, events and run policy tests.'
API contract specifies view_output_guard for POST /output-guard/:scope/test with { text, role?, policy? } and notes external checks run when includeExternal: true.
PolicyTester UI explicitly discloses that external checks (moderation / judge) may consume model calls, cost, and quota.
UI test explicitly verifies a view_output_guard-only actor running PolicyTester with includeExternal: true.

reason: Repository source refutes both the claimed root cause and the authorization premise. First, canCallGateway is strictly the capability gate for runJudgeCheck -> callGateway(ctx.req, ...) (which sends a loopback request to /v1/chat/completions carrying extractInferenceToken(req); see context.ts:158 canRunExternalJudge and support-adapter.ts:11-12). router.ts:272 passes canCallGateway: false unconditionally for all authenticated dashboard callers (including the primary admin) because dashboard session requests lack an inference API token; blocking runModerationCheck on canCallGateway === false would disable moderation on POST /output-guard/:scopeKind/:scopeId/test for every user including primary admins, contradicting testPolicy's explicit includeExternal and outputGuard pillar checks (policy.ts:390,446-455). Second, view_output_guard is explicitly designed, documented, and tested to run policy dry-run tests with inline policy and includeExternal: true (shared/permissions.ts:85, specs/018-ai-platform-upgrade/contracts/admin-api.md:75, output-guard-strings.ts:90-91 disclosing model call/cost/quota usage, and output-guard.test.tsx:299-350), while testPolicy never writes policy or guard-event records and runModerations restricts outbound targets to hardcoded moderation endpoints with monthly budget checks and sanitized responses.

title: Thruline provider account baseUrl bypasses SSRF checks at save time and via non-custom proxyFetch / bare fetch paths
description: Unlike /nodes and backup restore, Thruline account creation (POST /, /connect-free, /bulk) stores arbitrary baseUrl values via createApiKeyAccount without calling assessProviderUrl, and runtime consumers (fetch-models, x-gateway video/embeddings/speech/transcription/voices/image/media-test, OpenCode/OAuth BaseProvider paths, plus bare fetch() for searxng/ollama-search and opencode free-model discovery) either pass platform !== 'custom' to proxyFetch (skipping assertProviderUrlAllowed and redirect:'manual') or bypass proxyFetch entirely.
claimed_root_cause: createApiKeyAccount in server/src/custom/provider-accounts/store.ts:771-875 persists user-supplied baseUrl into x_gateway_keys without assessProviderUrl validation and only checks http(s) syntax for normalizedProvider === 'custom' (lines 797-814, persisted at line 859). At runtime, proxyFetch in server/src/lib/proxy.ts:858-879 only enforces assertProviderUrlAllowed and redirect:'manual' when platform === 'custom', while callers in server/src/custom/provider-accounts/router.ts:674, server/src/custom/x-gateway/protocols.ts:1171/1362/1460/1668/1782, server/src/custom/x-gateway/image-generation.ts:165/573/673/695, and server/src/custom/x-gateway/media-router.ts:389/496/593/697 pass account.platform !== 'custom' (resolved by platformForXGatewayProvider at catalog.ts:7670-7679), and non-custom BaseProviders constructed in catalog.ts:7727-7849 pass their own non-'custom' this.platform via BaseProvider.fetchWithTimeout (providers/base.ts:427). Additionally, nativeSearch for searxng (server/src/custom/x-gateway/router.ts:1709) and ollama-search (router.ts:1758), as well as fetchOpenCodeFreeModels in server/src/custom/provider-accounts/opencode.ts:361 (called from provider-accounts/router.ts:240), use bare fetch() with default redirect:'follow' and no URL guard.

trace.description: Accepts provider and baseUrl from authenticated users holding use_x_gateway + add_keys + manage_key_models (lines 52, 185-189) and passes them to createApiKeyAccount; the same pattern appears at /connect-free (lines 215-236, including searxng and opencode) and /bulk (lines 254-273).

Stores baseUrl in x_gateway_keys without assessProviderUrl(..., { blockPrivate: true }) (contrast provider-accounts/router.ts:299/323 and config-restore.ts:39) and without http(s) scheme validation when normalizedProvider !== 'custom' (lines 797-814); hydrateAccountRow (line 180) resolves account.platform via platformForXGatewayProvider (catalog.ts:7670-7679), producing non-'custom' platforms for registered providers (e.g., gemini->google, siliconflow, groq, mistral, nvidia, openrouter, huggingface, opencode).

Gated on use_x_gateway + view_keys (lines 52, 639), passes account.base_url and account.platform to proxyFetch, skipping lib/proxy.ts:858's platform==='custom' SSRF and redirect guard when account.platform !== 'custom'; the same non-custom proxyFetch pattern occurs in x-gateway/protocols.ts (lines 1171, 1362, 1460, 1668, 1782), image-generation.ts (lines 165, 573, 673, 695), media-router.ts (lines 389, 496, 593, 697), and BaseProvider instances from catalog.ts:7727-7849 via providers/base.ts:427, while searxng/ollama-search (x-gateway/router.ts:1709, 1758) and opencode free-model discovery (opencode.ts:361 via provider-accounts/router.ts:240) call bare fetch().

title: Extended OAuth completion accepts omitted state, unverified callback origins, missing PKCE, and raw access_token injection
description: Unlike native OAuth in subscription-router.ts which verifies callback origin, pathname, and state === a.id, completeExtendedOAuth in oauth-extended.ts checks state only when present, does not check pasted callback URL origins against attempt.redirectUri, omits PKCE on cline_callback and iflow_oauth (and state on cline_callback), and allows an access_token fallback.
claimed_root_cause: completeExtendedOAuth treats state as optional ('if (returnedState && returnedState !== attempt.state)'), omits redirectUri origin/pathname checks, omits PKCE on cline/iflow, and allows direct access_token fallback without state verification.

trace.description: Accepts code/callback payload from the caller after lookup(req) validates the session-bound attemptId and delegates extended OAuth attempts to completeExtendedOAuth (line 259).
When no code parameter is present, accepts direct accessToken/access_token in JSON or query params and returns a credential object without token exchange or state verification (lines 696-705).
Checks 'if (returnedState && returnedState !== attempt.state)', skipping state verification when state is omitted and not validating pasted callback URL origins against attempt.redirectUri.
Persists the resulting credential into x_gateway_keys via saveExtendedOAuthAccount.

evidence.description: Dashboard authentication reads session tokens exclusively from the Authorization Bearer or x-dashboard-token headers (never cookies/ambient credentials).
Frontend apiFetch reads the session token from localStorage and sends it as an explicit Authorization: Bearer header.
lookup(req) requires a valid 256-bit random attemptId bound to hash(req.sessionToken) and re-checks use_x_gateway plus add_keys or edit_keys permissions before completeExtendedOAuth runs.

AccountCallback only calls subscriptionApi.complete when both state starting with 'sub_' and code are present; omitted state or ?access_token without code does not submit to /subscriptions/:attemptId/complete.
No /oauth/callback route exists in the client router (unknown paths fall through to NotFoundPage); extended OAuth callbacks are pasted manually in SubscriptionConnectDialog.

title: Premature SSE client socket close triggers res.on('close') quota refund after tokens are streamed
description: Both enforceUsageQuota and enforceEndUserQuota treat a response 'close' event before 'finish' as a failed/aborted request refund and skip token recording and DB persistence (while userInferenceGate's recordUserUsage also fires only on 'finish'). During passthrough SSE streaming (e.g., POST /v1/chat/completions with stream:true, and identically on /v1/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses, /v1beta streamGenerateContent, and /thruline/v1/chat/completions), generated delta chunks are written incrementally to the response socket prior to res.end(). While non-refunded per-minute RPM limits (checkUserRateLimit and proxyRateLimitRpm, when configured) remain enforced, a client with a configured daily or monthly request/token quota (sk-cp- profile, sk-flm-/sk-xgw- user key, or X-End-User/body.user end user) can read streamed output tokens and destroy the TCP socket before [DONE]/res.end(), triggering res.on('close') before 'finish' to decrement the admitted request counter and omit token/DB accounting.
claimed_root_cause: server/src/custom/quota-gate.ts:39-40 and server/src/custom/end-user-gate.ts:41-42 bind res.on('finish', () => end(true)) and res.on('close', () => end(false)) behind a one-shot `ended` flag without checking whether headers or streamed output chunks were already flushed (or tracking streamed tokens). When passthrough SSE in server/src/routes/proxy.ts writes chunks via writeChunk (2869, 2890) and the client disconnects before res.end() (3060), Node emits 'close' while !res.writableEnded (2155-2160), causing end(false) to invoke admission.settle(false, 0) in server/src/services/usage-quotas.ts:139-143 and server/src/services/end-user-quotas.ts:76-80, decrementing day.requests/month.requests and skipping token additions and DB counter upserts (while server/src/lib/fallback-loop.ts:1597-1609 exits on client abort without calling res.end() or emitting 'finish').

trace.description: Admits sk-cp- profile and end-user requests (and userInferenceGate in server/src/middleware/user-rate-limit.ts:106 admits sk-flm-/sk-xgw- user requests) for POST /v1/chat/completions with stream: true, registering res.on('finish') and res.on('close') settlement listeners before forwarding via proceed() / next().

Transitions to passthrough mode on the first non-dialect/non-JSON delta, flushes SSE headers (2889), and writes streamed token deltas directly to res via writeChunk (2869, 2890) prior to res.end() (3060), while client socket disconnect triggers res.on('close') with !res.writableEnded (2155-2160), setting clientGone and aborting upstream (2756, 3110) so server/src/lib/fallback-loop.ts:1597-1609 exits without calling res.end().

Fires end(false) before 'finish' and locks `ended = true`, refunding day.requests/month.requests in server/src/services/usage-quotas.ts:139-143 (and identically in server/src/services/end-user-quotas.ts:76-80 via server/src/custom/end-user-gate.ts:42) while recording 0 tokens and skipping custom_usage_counters / custom_end_user_counters persistence.

Identical request decrement and early return skipping custom_end_user_counters persistence when succeeded is false.
Passthrough SSE mode writes delta content chunks incrementally via writeChunk (2869, 2890) prior to res.end() at line 3060, while res.on('close') (2155-2160) aborts clientAbort on !res.writableEnded.

title: Unscoped response cache key allows cross-user and cross-profile cache bleed and X-FreeLLM-Cache oracle/poisoning

Server runs a single Node.js HTTP process via app.listen without node:cluster or DB-accessing worker_threads.

reason: Source refutes the claimed concurrent-request race and local interleaving prerequisite. In Node.js, checkAndConsumeSupportUserQuota and its sole HTTP caller POST /thruline/v1/support/guardrails/check execute completely synchronously with zero await or event-loop yield points between readStore (line 365) and writeStore (line 393), and all three repository DB backends (better-sqlite3, node:sqlite, and the synchronous libsql Turso wrapper) execute statements synchronously while blocking the single event loop. title: Support SQL sandbox regex table-rewrite and column filter bypassed by parenthesized table joins and allowedColumns aliasing
description: validateAndRewriteSupportSql in server/src/custom/x-gateway/support-connectors.ts discovers tables and enforces allowedRoles, rowOwnerColumn filtering, deniedColumns checks, and stripHiddenColumns via a regex (refRe) requiring an unparenthesized identifier directly after FROM or JOIN. title: assessProviderUrl resolves DNS before unpinned fetch(), enabling DNS-rebinding TOCTOU across SSRF guards
description: Outbound SSRF protection in assessProviderUrl (server/src/lib/url-guard.ts:215-271) resolves the target hostname via dns.promises.lookup, validates IP address classes, and returns only { allowed: true } without capturing or binding the validated IP into an undici dispatcher. Strongest existing controls on the path include metadata/link-local classification (including IPv4-mapped/compatible, NAT64, and trailing-dot metadata names), fail-closed behavior on unresolvable DNS at request time, opt-in private/loopback blocking (always enabled for /thruline/v1/fetch via { blockPrivate: true } at router.ts:2143, off by default elsewhere unless FREEAPI_BLOCK_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS is set), and manual/hop-rechecked redirects (proxy.ts:867, 873-879; google.ts:359-373; media.ts:310-331; router.ts:2156-2172). By comparison, safeFetch in server/src/custom/x-gateway/support-safe-http.ts:568-603, 645-735 avoids this TOCTOU pattern in the same codebase by pinning resolvedIps in an undici.Agent lookup function.

title: Serverless fetch-relay templates deployed via proxy-pool omit caller authentication
description: All four serverless HTTP relay templates in server/src/custom/x-gateway/proxy-pool.ts (CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_RELAY_CODE, VERCEL_RELAY_CODE, DENO_RELAY_CODE, and NETLIFY_RELAY_CODE) strip the fetch-relay-authorization header without validating any bearer token or shared secret and forward caller-supplied fetch-relay-target requests to fetch(). title: downloadProviderImage follows arbitrary HTTP redirects without hop-by-hop allowlist or SSRF validation

title: Multipart STT and media-default fallback bypass per-key allowedModels restrictions in x-gateway protocols
description: On POST /thruline/v1/audio/transcriptions, xGatewayAuth runs before Multer parses the multipart/form-data body, while upstream express.json() middleware leaves req.body undefined for multipart uploads. Consequently, xGatewayAuth evaluates isModelAllowedForKey against 'auto' instead of the submitted form field. If a restricted sk-xgw key permits 'auto' (e.g., allowedModels=['auto'] or ['auto','whisper-1']), the request passes auth, Multer populates req.body.model, and the transcription handler forwards the caller-chosen model (including disallowed provider/model or combo selectors) via resolveCandidateRoutes and proxyFetch without re-checking isModelAllowedForKey. In addition, /embeddings, /images/generations, /audio/speech, and /audio/transcriptions expand 'auto' to getMediaDefaults().*.defaultModel without re-checking isModelAllowedForKey against the resolved default model.

title: Public skills endpoints reflect untrusted Host and X-Forwarded-Proto into AI agent setup commands with Cache-Control: public
description: extractOrigin(req) in server/src/custom/x-gateway/skills-router.ts constructs an origin string directly from unvalidated req.get('host') and raw req.get('x-forwarded-proto'), bypassing Express's trust proxy setting (which defaults to false) and performing no scheme, host, or URL-delimiter validation (unlike canonical PUBLIC_APP_URL validation elsewhere in the codebase). Public unauthenticated routes /thruline-skills/:id, /thruline-skills/:id/SKILL.md, and their /x-skills aliases mounted via registerCustomRoutes substitute this origin into {{GATEWAY_URL}}, ${GATEWAY_URL}, and $GATEWAY_URL in skill markdown containing shell exports and curl commands carrying Authorization: Bearer ${GATEWAY_KEY}, and return Cache-Control: public, max-age=60 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and no Vary header covering Host or X-Forwarded-Proto (under createApp(), cors() only sets Vary: Origin when Origin is omitted or allowed). When ALLOWED_HOSTS is unset (the default), any Host header passes createHostGuard; even when ALLOWED_HOSTS is enabled, X-Forwarded-Proto remains unvalidated. In deployments fronted by a shared cache or CDN that caches public responses without keying on Host (including port) and X-Forwarded-Proto and forwards untrusted values, poisoned skill documents could direct AI agents to send bearer tokens and prompts to an attacker-controlled origin.

title: Thruline Gemini mounts (/thruline/v1beta, /x/v1beta, /v1beta) bypass userInferenceGate limits/attribution, proxy rate limiter, and disabled-gateway guard
